tldr: Cognex reported Q4 2025 revenue of $252M (+10% YoY) and adjusted diluted EPS of $0.27 (+35%), capping a turnaround year with full-year revenue of $994M (+9%) and adjusted EBITDA margin of 21.5% (20.7% excluding the one-time commercial partnership). Management paired Q1 2026 guidance of $235M-$255M revenue and $0.22-$0.26 adjusted EPS with portfolio pruning (~$22M revenue) and a $35M-$40M annualized cost-reduction plan targeting a 25% adjusted EBITDA run-rate by year-end 2026.
bullets: Q4 2025 results: revenue $252M (+10% YoY, +9% constant currency), adjusted EBITDA margin 22.7% (+420 bps YoY), and adjusted diluted EPS $0.27 (+35% YoY); management cited strong year-end factory automation demand and steady logistics growth.

FY2025 results: revenue $994M (+9% as reported; +8% constant currency), adjusted EBITDA margin 21.5% (+440 bps), and adjusted diluted EPS $1.02 (+38%); excluding the one-time commercial partnership, revenue was $982M (+7%), adjusted EBITDA margin was 20.7%, and adjusted EPS was $0.97.

Capital and outlook: FY2025 free cash flow was $237M (+77% YoY; 138% conversion on adjusted net income), year-end cash and investments were $642M with no debt, and Q1 2026 guidance calls for revenue of $235M-$255M, adjusted EBITDA margin of 19.0%-22.0%, and adjusted diluted EPS of $0.22-$0.26.
themes: Asset visibility and data capture adoption expanding
Industrial and logistics demand uneven by region
Pricing and cost pressure shaping margins
Portfolio shifts and M&A reshaping focus

segments.title: Q4 and FY2025 turnaround execution
points: Q4 revenue rose to $252M (+10% YoY; +9% constant currency), GAAP operating margin was 14.0%, and adjusted EBITDA margin reached 22.7%, above the guided range midpoint and the sixth straight quarter of year-over-year expansion.
Q4 adjusted diluted EPS was $0.27 (+35% YoY) and GAAP diluted EPS was $0.19 (+18% YoY), driven by revenue growth, cost discipline, and a lower diluted share count.
FY2025 revenue was $994M (+9% YoY), GAAP operating margin was 16.3%, adjusted EBITDA margin was 21.5%, and adjusted diluted EPS was $1.02 (+38% YoY).

segments.title: Portfolio optimization and operating model actions
points: Management said Cognex completed a portfolio review and started exiting approximately $22M of non-core, no-growth or low-margin revenue, including a Japan-focused trading business and product lines such as Mobile SDK and Edge Intelligence.
The company identified an additional $35M-$40M of annualized cost reductions by end-2026 and reiterated a 25% adjusted EBITDA margin run-rate target exiting 2026.
Cognex raised its through-cycle adjusted EBITDA margin range to 25%-31% (from 20%-30%), while keeping through-cycle revenue CAGR at 13%-14% and free cash flow conversion above 100%.

segments.title: End-market and regional demand signals
points: 2025 trends were strongest in logistics, consumer electronics, packaging, and semiconductor, while automotive remained weak; for 2026, management framed an initial view of mid-single- to high-single-digit growth overall rather than formal full-year guidance.

By end market (deck): logistics was 26% of 2025 revenue and expected to moderate to mid- to high-single-digit growth in 2026 after two outsized years; consumer electronics was 19% of revenue and expected at high-single- to double-digit growth.

Q4 regional commentary indicated Americas constant-currency revenue grew 11%, Europe 13%, Greater China 7%, and Other Asia was flat; automotive recovery was described as strongest in the Americas, slowest in Europe, and mixed in Asia.

segments.title: Cash generation and capital deployment
points: FY2025 operating cash flow was $246M (+65% YoY) and free cash flow was $237M (+77% YoY), with free cash flow conversion of 138% versus adjusted net income.
Cognex returned $206M to shareholders in 2025, including $151M of repurchases and $55M of dividends.

As of December 31, 2025, Cognex had $642M in cash and investments and no debt; the board added $500M to the repurchase authorization on February 11, 2026 and declared a quarterly dividend of $0.085 per share.

guidance.note: revenue CAGR 13%-14% and free cash flow conversion >100%

notes.title: Q4 one-time items and non-GAAP treatment
points: Management referenced a $5M gain from sale of a Natick property and a $13M excess-and-obsolete inventory charge; both were excluded from non-GAAP results.
Press release reconciliations show reported GAAP gross margin of 65.7% and adjusted gross margin of 71.6% in Q4 2025.

notes.title: Divestment timing and vertical mix impact
points: In Q&A, management said most of the ~$22M exiting revenue is the Japan-focused trading business and expects the transaction to close by Q2 2026, with P&L effects largely in 2H 2026.
Management said the exited revenue is mainly in packaging and, to a lesser extent, logistics, while keeping the same growth expectations for those verticals on a lower base.

notes.title: Working capital and cash conversion
points: Management said the cash conversion cycle improved by 57 days year over year (116 days from the 2023 peak), supporting FY2025 free cash flow growth.
For 2026, management expects less incremental benefit from working-capital optimization but still expects free cash flow conversion to remain above 100%, supported by margin expansion.

themes.title: Portfolio exits: scope, timing, and growth-base reset
points: Analysts asked how the ~$22M revenue exit flows through guidance and vertical assumptions.

Management said the largest piece is the Japan trading divestment targeted to close by Q2 2026, with most impact showing in 2H 2026, and suggested modeling 2026 growth off a 2025 base net of exited revenue.

themes.title: 2026 demand view versus Q1 guide
points: Questions focused on reconciling the +13% Q1 midpoint growth guide with a broader mid-single- to high-single-digit 2026 demand view.
Management attributed the Q1 setup to year-end spending timing shifts and a weak Q1 2025 comparison, while emphasizing limited visibility in a short-cycle business.

themes.title: Margin bridge and cost-out cadence
points: Investors pressed on offsets to the $35M-$40M cost program and the cadence of margin benefits.
Management described OpEx efficiency as the primary lever, with mix as a partial headwind, and said most execution happens in 1H 2026 with clearer financial effects expected by Q3.

themes.title: End-market drivers and regional variance
points: Q&A probed logistics moderation, CE demand drivers, and automotive recovery by geography.

Management cited CE demand from refresh cycles, AI-enabled device features, and supply-chain shifts; logistics remains positive but normalizing after eight quarters of double-digit growth; automotive was described as stronger in the Americas, weakest in Europe, and mixed in Asia.

themes.title: Supply chain cost risk
points: Analysts asked about memory pricing and procurement risk.
Management said no material memory-related cost impact is currently expected and indicated the current outlook already reflects observed supply conditions.

top_questions.question: How should investors model the ~$22M non-core revenue exit in 2026?
top_questions.summary: Management said most of the exit is the Japan-focused trading business expected to close in Q2 2026; they advised applying 2026 growth assumptions to a 2025 revenue base net of the exited business.

top_questions.question: Is the Q1 midpoint growth of +13% a sign of stronger full-year acceleration?
top_questions.summary: Management said Q1 is influenced by timing shifts from late-2025 spending and a weak prior-year quarter, so they still framed 2026 as an initial mid-single- to high-single-digit growth view rather than full-year guidance.

top_questions.question: What offsets the $35M-$40M cost savings in the 2026 margin bridge?
top_questions.summary: The company cited favorable 2025 mix that is not fully recurring as a headwind, partially mitigated by portfolio actions and potential pricing stability/tailwind, with OpEx efficiency still the dominant lever.

top_questions.question: What is driving consumer electronics and logistics demand entering 2026?
top_questions.summary: Management pointed to CE supply-chain relocation, new device form factors, and AI-feature-driven refresh demand, while describing logistics as still healthy but moderating after an extended period of outsized growth.

top_questions.question: Are higher memory costs becoming a material risk to 2026 guidance?
top_questions.summary: Management said memory has not been a material headwind so far and that procurement conditions are manageable with current supplier relationships and planning practices.

implications: Cognex is positioning AI-enabled machine vision as a workflow productivity lever across logistics and factory automation, with management highlighting broader use cases beyond barcode reading (for example, tunnel standardization plus added vision applications).
The salesforce transformation signal (9,000 new accounts added in 2025 versus roughly 3,000 in 2024) suggests broader account penetration potential in underpenetrated markets such as packaging.

Management's decision to exit low-growth/low-margin lines and target 25% adjusted EBITDA run-rate by year-end 2026 indicates a deliberate shift toward higher-quality recurring demand pockets rather than maximizing headline revenue.
Semiconductor commentary tied to an AI-driven investment cycle supports the case that upstream AI infrastructure spending is feeding demand for high-precision industrial inspection tools.
competitive_notes: Management highlighted a nearly decade-long AI machine vision buildout plus 2025 launches (DataMan 290, In-Sight 8900, OneVision, SLX), indicating active product-cycle competition in ID, factory automation, and logistics automation.

Portfolio pruning around Moritex-linked trading and selected non-core software/tools suggests Cognex is prioritizing categories where it believes it has stronger IP differentiation and better long-term margin structure.
forecast_hooks: Track whether the Japan-focused trading divestment closes in Q2 2026 and how much of the ~$22M revenue exit is visible in 2H 2026 reported mix.
Watch for Q3 2026 evidence that first-half cost actions are converting into the targeted year-end 25% adjusted EBITDA run-rate.

Monitor whether logistics growth stabilizes in the guided mid- to high-single-digit band after two years of double-digit growth, and whether CE momentum remains strong through seasonal Q2/Q3 patterns.
Check if pricing remains stable/tailwind as management expects, given tariffs and mix effects discussed in Q4 and FY2025 commentary.

action_items: Reconcile 2026 quarterly models to management's base-reset approach (2025 revenue less exited ~$22M business) and confirm when divestment timing is reflected in segment/end-market disclosures.
Track quarterly progression of adjusted EBITDA margin toward the 25% exit-rate target and separate OpEx savings from mix-driven impacts.
Monitor end-market updates for logistics, CE, automotive, and semiconductor against the initial 2026 view ranges disclosed in the deck.
open_questions: Will the announced $35M-$40M cost actions deliver mostly in-year 2026 benefit, or will a larger share annualize into 2027?
How durable is CE growth if the current AI-device refresh cycle cools later in 2026?
Can pricing remain a tailwind if tariff exposure or regional mix shifts become less favorable?
watch_next_quarter: Any formal update to full-year 2026 guidance posture versus the current 'initial view' framing.
Progress on closing the Japan-focused trading divestment and any incremental portfolio cleanup actions.
Q1-to-Q2 revenue timing normalization and implications for logistics and broader factory automation demand visibility.
